newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds trade mixed, lacking strong direction.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds trade mixed, lacking strong direction.

text.p: Irish government bonds seesawed in late trade on Friday lacking inspiration due to a dearth of international data, dealers said.
Dealers said they expected the market to continue to trade within narrow ranges ahead of the publication of the Irish Central Bank's annual monetary policy statement on Tuesday.
"Ireland is marginally out-performing Germany which has been very extremely quiet," one dealer said. "At this stage we are looking ahead to Irish inflation data on Tuesday."

By 1610 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down five pence from Thursday's close at 103.20 to yield 5.68 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond was up two pence at 111.27 to yield 6.37 percent.
Dealers said Irish bonds were trading at 136 basis points over German bunds in the five-year area and 83 basis points over Germany in the 10-year area.
